profile.name: Matthew Hendricks
profile.tagline: tinycrops — self-directed research on machines that model themselves, and can show it to someone else
profile.blurb: Independent research run on a five-machine cluster of secondhand hardware: local model serving, embedding stores, brain-response modelling, ASR and voice. Everything below is public and reproducible, including the experiments that failed.

selected.title: Why viewers stay — brain-response retention report
selected.note: Ran 99 of a creator's TikToks through Meta FAIR's TRIBE v2, a model trained on fMRI paired with video that predicts second-by-second cortical activation, then compared its predictions against that account's real audience-retention curves. A neuroscience encoding model used as a practical tool for a working creator.

selected.title: TRIBE v2 Brain Response Gallery
selected.note: Predicts fMRI cortical activation for the opening 15 seconds of a video across 20,484 fsaverage5 vertices, stacking V-JEPA2 for vision, Wav2Vec-BERT for audio and LLaMA 3.2 for speech, then reads the result out over the 76 named Destrieux regions as a browsable heatmap.

selected.title: Mercenary Warrant price-check — upstream feature
selected.note: Built a price-check path for a new item class in a trading tool with a large user base, ported from an upstream issue and verified end to end against live trade data.

selected.title: How many bits is a person?
selected.note: Tests whether personality is a small, low-dimensional handle across six independent datasets — 22,940+ users in KuaiRand, 1,200 blog authors, 167 nations in FAOSTAT, plus World Bank, Hofstede and food embeddings. Lands on roughly 4 to 16 bits, about two dimensions, and argues it must be carried because more compute cannot re-derive it.

selected.title: The Gemini Manifold Book
selected.note: A public measurement book for multimodal embeddings, one chapter per experiment, embeddings stored so results can be checked. The driving question: does a model read an ASCII cathedral as text, as image, or as something that bridges both?

selected.title: The Realness Ladder
selected.note: Measures whether ASCII art, rasterized and pushed through an img2img bridge, moves monotonically toward photographic realness in a shared embedding space. It does, across a nine-subject corpus, and subject identity survives the whole ladder.

selected.title: A model that draws computers on computers
selected.note: An 11.9M-parameter character-level nGPT trained on 9.2M tokens, primed with nothing but a start token and left to emit one character at a time until it decides to stop — testing whether self-similar training teaches image-like text generation.

selected.title: Geometry as Judge
selected.note: Asks whether the geometry of an embedding space can stand in for a human rater. Keeps the negative results in view — where the geometry disagrees with people, and why that matters more than where it agrees.

selected.title: ARC orientation workbench
selected.note: A corpus-level workbench for ARC-AGI built on one primitive — nuisance, group action, harmonic invariants. Retrieval accuracy moved from 28% to 46% under that framing.

selected.title: OKF Commons — compressed research memory
selected.note: Turns years of saved browser tabs into a queryable knowledge base with bidirectional provenance, so every claim traces back to the source that produced it.

selected.title: articulate — get the computer out of the way
selected.note: Turns a recorded thought into a finished captioned vertical essay, assembling narration, captions, slides and cuts from speech alone. Built for the case where the idea was never the hard part — the editing was.

selected.title: Land siting by constraint scoring
selected.note: Scored and shortlisted 26 land candidates across 8 Western New York counties on water distance, road distance, slope, floodplain and wetland balance. Included as evidence the same method transfers outside machine learning.
